=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:`_unsafe_conflict_path_category` (function body, the `parts = PurePosixPath(name).parts if name else ()` line that runs before the `"\x00" in name` guard) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The function computes `PurePosixPath(name).parts` before the explicit NUL-byte check, but `pathlib.PurePosixPath` raises `ValueError: embedded null byte` for any name containing `\x00`.
  WHY: `check_paths` rejects a NUL-bearing conflicted name through the `except LookupError` branch. `_host_only_or_unsafe` short-circuits on the `REPORTABLE_PATH_RE` regex mismatch and returns `"unsafe"` without ever calling `PurePosixPath`. The handler then calls `_unsafe_conflict_path_category(host, name)` to compute the new `unsafe<TAB><category><TAB><depth>` entry. That call re-enters the NUL path: `PurePosixPath(name).parts` raises `ValueError`, the new exception fires from inside the active `except` handler, no surrounding `except` catches it, and the resolver aborts with an unhandled exception on the input class the PR explicitly promises to handle ("Never walk the host for a name that could leave the checkout"). The previous version handled `ValueError` by appending the bare `unsafe` token; the LAST RUN moved the diagnostic computation outside the try block, making NUL-bearing paths a regression.
